rows.description: A team builds trust when members do small things they promised, admit errors early and share credit. Trust is earned in ordinary moments, not in team-building slogans.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Resolving conflict with facts and feelings [Response]
rows.description: A mature colleague names the issue, states the effect on them and asks for the other's view. They look for a shared solution, without needing to be proven right.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtopic: Family systems (joint family, in-laws, favourite child, family roles and secrets)
rows.subtype: Reading the mood of the household [Actor]
rows.description: A young child senses tension between adults and becomes quiet, clingy or extra good. Children adapt to the family's emotional weather long before they understand its cause.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtopic: Family systems (joint family, in-laws, favourite child, family roles and secrets)
rows.subtype: Growing up in a joint family [Receiver]
rows.description: A child in a joint household has many caregivers, cousins for play and many opinions about their behaviour. They gain warmth and belonging and lose some privacy and a single clear voice of authority.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtopic: Family systems (joint family, in-laws, favourite child, family roles and secrets)
rows.description: A child who is openly preferred enjoys the praise and feels guilty or uneasy about a sibling's hurt. They may also feel pressure to keep earning the position.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: anxiety, guilt, hurt

rows.subtopic: Family systems (joint family, in-laws, favourite child, family roles and secrets)
rows.description: A child who is compared unfavourably with a brother or sister feels quietly invisible. They may work harder for approval, rebel or withdraw, and often carry the comparison into adult life.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtopic: Family systems (joint family, in-laws, favourite child, family roles and secrets)
rows.subtype: Family roles: the responsible one and the troublemaker [Actor]
rows.description: A teenager fits a role the family assigned, such as the reliable one, the funny one or the problem. The role brings a place in the family and also limits who they are allowed to become.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtopic: Family systems (joint family, in-laws, favourite child, family roles and secrets)
rows.description: A teenager senses that something is not discussed, such as a debt, an illness or a relative's history. Unspoken secrets make children anxious and imaginative, and they often guess worse than the truth.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtopic: Family systems (joint family, in-laws, favourite child, family roles and secrets)
rows.subtype: Caught between parents and own choices [Actor]
rows.description: A young adult feels duty to family expectations about career or marriage and desire for their own path. They feel both loyal and resentful, and neither feeling cancels the other.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtopic: Family systems (joint family, in-laws, favourite child, family roles and secrets)
rows.subtype: Stepping out of a fixed family role [Response]
rows.description: A young adult quietly stops playing the peacemaker or the rebel and responds as themselves. The family may resist at first, and steady, kind consistency usually allows the system to adjust.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
